mainTopic: Leaving versus returning food on a כירה on שבת, leaning a pot against an unswept stove, and a covered stove that flared up again.
overview: The גמרא asks whether the first clause of the כירה משנה is about leaving food on the stove (לשהות) or putting it back (להחזיר). It turns back a proof for לשהות by saying the משנה has missing words (חסורי מחסרא). It then turns back רבי חלבו's rule ('on top, not inside') as a proof for להחזיר, because that rule may refer to the סיפא. A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה report בית שמאי and בית הלל differently seems to favor לשהות. The גמרא answers that the משנה can still be about returning if our תנא agrees with רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another. The question is defended but never decided. Next the גמרא asks whether one may lean a pot against an unswept stove. After two proofs are pushed off and one push-off is challenged, a ברייתא rules that leaning is allowed and only leaving on top needs a swept or covered stove. The amud ends with רב אושעיא's rule: on a covered stove that flared up again, fully cooked food may be left.

steps.title: Rejecting the earlier proof by filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof for לשהות. It says the משנה really is about להחזיר and has words missing. It then rebuilds the full text: returning food needs a swept stove, but leaving food is allowed even on an unswept one. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about what may be left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you the משנה is about returning, and some words are missing. Here is what it means: on a stove heated with straw or stubble, you may return cooked food. On one heated with olive waste or wood, you may not return food until you sweep out the coals or cover them with ash. But leaving food there is allowed even if the stove was not swept or covered. And what may be left? בית שמאי say hot water but not cooked food, and בית הלל say hot water and cooked food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending the 'returning' reading by saying the משנה left some words out. It then writes out the full version of what the משנה supposedly means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof argued that the משנה's later line 'בית הלל say: one may even return' shows the first clause must be about leaving. The answer here is that the first clause is about returning, and a separate missing line about leaving was dropped. That missing line is what בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about (hot water vs. cooked food).

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words, and we fill them in
To put the pot back on the stove on שבת
To leave a pot on the stove from before שבת
Swept out (coals removed) and covered with ash
Olive waste left after pressing; it burns very hot
Straw and stubble; weak fuels

steps.confusionAlert: Under this rebuilt version, the stricter rule (you must sweep or cover) is for returning food. Leaving food is more lenient and is allowed even on an unswept stove.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you: we learned 'to return,'
and the text is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
A stove that was heated with straw or stubble —
one may return cooked food onto it;
with olive waste or wood — one may not return

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּגְרוֹף אוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן אֶת הָאֵפֶר.
phrases.english: until he sweeps it or until he puts ash on it.
But to leave food — one may leave it

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ גָּרוּף וְאֵינוֹ קָטוּם.
phrases.english: even though it is not swept and not covered with ash.
And what may they leave?

phrases.aramaic: — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water, but not cooked food.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and cooked food.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ לְהַחֲזִיר תְּנַן, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for לשהות brought on the previous amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question itself (לשהות or להחזיר) stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's text is complete. If words are missing, the 'returning' reading still works.

steps.title: The returning law is itself a dispute
steps.stepSummary: Still rebuilding the משנה, the גמרא explains that the permission to return food in the first clause is not agreed on by everyone. בית שמאי forbid returning and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the returning I told you about is not everyone's opinion. It is a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל: בית שמאי say you may take the food off but not put it back, and בית הלל say you may even put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rebuilt version of the משנה. It explains why the משנה ends with 'בית הלל say: one may even return.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the question the earlier proof raised. The line 'אף מחזירין' is not repeating the first clause. It tells us that the first clause, which allows returning, follows only בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone's opinion; agreed by all
One may take the food off the stove
One may put the food back

steps.whatToRemember: Under the 'returning' reading, the משנה has two separate disputes: what may be left (hot water vs. cooked food) and whether food may be returned. The question is still not settled.

phrases.english: And that returning that I told you about
is not everyone's opinion;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַחֲלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: rather, it is a dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין וְלֹא מַחֲזִירִין.
phrases.english: for Beit Shammai say: one may remove but not return.
And Beit Hillel say: one may even return.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָךְ חֲזָרָה דַּאֲמַרִי לָךְ, לָאו דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rebuilt משנה begun in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the rejection of the earlier proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'אף מחזירין' line can be read as naming who holds the returning permission, not as a sign that the first clause is about leaving.

steps.title: Proof from רבי חלבו: on top is allowed, inside is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי חלבו's report in the name of רב: the משנה's permission applies only to placing food on top of the stove, not inside it. That difference makes sense for returning food, but not for leaving it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא, in the name of רב: they taught this only for on top of the stove, but inside it is forbidden. If the משנה is about returning, that explains why inside and on top are different. But if it is about leaving, what difference does inside or on top make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof, this time for the 'returning' reading, using an אמורא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a pot back inside a stove on שבת is more like cooking, so a line between inside and on top fits returning. When food is only being left there, nothing new is done on שבת, so where the pot sits should not matter. That suggests רב was talking about returning.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא is bringing a proof
They taught this only for...
On top of the stove
Inside the stove
It makes sense if you say...

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Ḥelbo said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
They taught this only regarding on top of it,
but inside it — it is forbidden.
It makes sense if you say we learned 'to return' —

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּשָׁנֵי בֵּין תּוֹכָהּ לְעַל גַּבָּהּ.
phrases.english: that is why there is a difference between inside it and on top of it.
But if you say we learned 'to leave,'

phrases.aramaic: מַה לִּי תּוֹכָהּ מַה לִּי עַל גַּבָּהּ?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me, inside it or on top of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for לשהות failed, a new proof for להחזיר is brought.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's first clause is about להחזיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חלבו citing רב: allowed only on top, forbidden inside.

steps.title: רבי חלבו was talking about the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבי חלבו's rule does not explain the first clause. It explains the סיפא, 'בית הלל say: one may even return,' and limits that permission to on top of the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think רבי חלבו is talking about the first clause? He is talking about the last clause: 'And בית הלל say: one may even return.' On that, רבי חלבו said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא, in the name of רב: they taught this only for on top of the stove, but inside it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from רבי חלבו by moving his statement to a different line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does contain a returning law in its סיפא, so the 'on top, not inside' rule can belong there. That tells us nothing about whether the first clause is about leaving or returning, so the question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? (introduces a rejection)
Refers to the first clause
Refers to the last clause

phrases.aramaic: — מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי?
phrases.english: Do you think Rabbi Ḥelbo refers to the first clause?
He refers to the last clause:
'And Beit Hillel say: one may even return' —

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ḥelbo said that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
They taught this only regarding on top of it,
but inside it — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי? אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי חלבו in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from רבי חלבו. רב's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the statement was about the רישא. It can just as well be about the סיפא, which already deals with returning.

steps.title: A ברייתא on two adjoining stoves: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about two stoves joined together, one swept and one not. Food may be left only on the swept one. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each report the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: two stoves joined together, one swept and covered and one not swept and not covered. You may leave food on the swept, covered one, but not on the other. What may be left? בית שמאי say: nothing at all. בית הלל say: hot water but not cooked food. If the food was taken off, everyone agrees it may not be returned. This is רבי מאיר's version. רבי יהודה says: בית שמאי say hot water but not cooked food, and בית הלל say hot water and cooked food. בית שמאי say you may take it off but not return it, and בית הלל say you may even return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא. This step sets up the proof that comes next by laying out two versions of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions are about a swept and covered stove. רבי מאיר's version is stricter: בית שמאי allow nothing, בית הלל allow only hot water, and nobody allows returning. רבי יהודה's version matches our משנה's wording almost exactly: hot water vs. cooked food, and taking off vs. returning.

keyTerms.meaning: Two stoves joined side by side
Nothing at all
He took the pot off the stove
A תנא; gives the strict version
A תנא; gives the lenient version that matches the משנה's wording

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are not giving their own opinions. Each is reporting a different tradition of what בית שמאי and בית הלל said.

phrases.english: Come and hear: two adjoining stoves,
one swept and covered with ash,
and one not swept and not covered:
one may leave food on the swept and covered one

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְשַׁהִין עַל שֶׁאֵינָהּ גְּרוּפָה וְאֵינָהּ קְטוּמָה.
phrases.english: and one may not leave food on the one not swept and not covered.
And what may they leave?
Beit Shammai say: nothing at all.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: hot water, but not cooked food.
If he removed it — all agree he may not return it;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says —

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: חַמִּין, אֲבָל לֹא תַּבְשִׁיל.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: hot water, but not cooked food.
And Beit Hillel say: hot water and cooked food.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹטְלִין, אֲבָל לֹא מַחֲזִירִין.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: one may remove, but not return.
And Beit Hillel say: one may even return.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from רבי חלבו failed, a ברייתא is brought as a new source.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's first clause is about לשהות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the two adjoining stoves, with רבי מאיר's and רבי יהודה's versions.

steps.title: The leaving reading fits רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about leaving food, it fits רבי יהודה's version in the ברייתא well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say we learned 'to leave': whose view is our משנה? It is רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins using the ברייתא as a proof. It first shows that the 'leaving' reading has a clear source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the 'leaving' reading, the משנה allows leaving food only on a swept stove. בית שמאי and בית הלל then argue about hot water vs. cooked food, and about whether food may be returned. That is exactly רבי יהודה's version, which also deals with a swept stove.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is our משנה?

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say we learned 'to leave':
whose is our Mishnah? It is Rabbi Yehuda's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא ״לְשַׁהוֹת״ תְּנַן, מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 5 to the 'leaving' reading.
steps.raayaObject: The לשהות reading has a known תנא behind it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's version in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The returning reading fits neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about returning, no תנא fits it. It clashes with רבי מאיר once on בית שמאי and twice on בית הלל. It also clashes with רבי יהודה on the need for a swept and covered stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say we learned 'to return,' whose view is our משנה? It is neither רבי יהודה's nor רבי מאיר's. If it is רבי מאיר's, there is one problem with בית שמאי and two with בית הלל. If it is רבי יהודה's, there is a problem with the swept and covered stove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'returning' reading leaves the משנה without any matching תנא. That makes it a weak reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the returning reading, the משנה lets בית שמאי leave hot water. רבי מאיר says they allow nothing, which is one clash. The משנה also has בית הלל allowing cooked food and returning, while רבי מאיר says only hot water and no returning, which is two clashes. Finally, the משנה would allow leaving food on an unswept stove, but רבי יהודה's dispute is about a swept and covered stove.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a problem on one point
On two points
Neither... nor...

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא pushes toward reading the משנה as לשהות, because only that reading matches a known תנא (רבי יהודה).
steps.whyThisMatters: A reading of a משנה that matches no known תנא is hard to accept, so this is a strong argument for the לשהות reading.

phrases.english: But if you say we learned 'to return,'
whose is our Mishnah?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר — קַשְׁיָא לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: If Rabbi Meir — it is difficult for Beit Shammai in one respect,
and for Beit Hillel in two.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, קַשְׁיָא גְּרוּפָה וּקְטוּמָה.
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yehuda — the swept and covered stove is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ ״לְהַחֲזִיר״ תְּנַן, מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof from the ברייתא by showing the other reading fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: The להחזיר reading of the משנה, as rebuilt in steps 1-2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the משנה's views of בית שמאי and בית הלל do not match רבי מאיר's report. Its leniency about an unswept stove does not match רבי יהודה's setting of a swept and covered stove.

steps.title: The משנה is about returning, and its תנא partly agrees with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. The משנה really is about returning food. Its תנא follows רבי יהודה's version on one point but disagrees with him on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I can tell you that our משנה is about returning food. Our תנא agrees with רבי יהודה in one matter and disagrees with him in one matter. He agrees about hot water and cooked food, and about what may be taken off and what may be put back. He disagrees about leaving food: our תנא allows leaving it even on a stove that is not swept or covered, while רבי יהודה says even leaving needs a swept or covered stove, and otherwise it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7, which said that no תנא fits the משנה if it is about returning. It says our תנא follows רבי יהודה partly, not completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה matches רבי יהודה's report of the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל: whether hot water and cooked food are allowed, and whether one may take off and put back. Our תנא splits from רבי יהודה on one point only. He holds that leaving food does not need a swept or covered stove; only returning does. So the משנה does have a תנא after all: someone who mostly follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you: a formula for keeping the original reading and answering the challenge
Our תנא, the author of our משנה

keyTerms.term: סָבַר לַהּ כְּ... בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
keyTerms.meaning: He agrees with him in one matter and disagrees with him in one matter
Swept clean of coals, or with the coals covered by ashes
One may take off and put back

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's last word here keeps the 'returning' reading alive: under it, a swept or covered stove is needed only to put food back, and leaving food is allowed even without one. This partly follows רבי יהודה. This answer defends the reading against the ברייתא's challenge. It does not prove that the משנה must be about returning, and the גמרא moves on to a new question without ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה follows רבי יהודה completely. It agrees with him about which foods are allowed and about taking off and returning. It disagrees with him about whether leaving food needs a swept stove.

phrases.english: Really, I can tell you: we learned 'to return'

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא דִידַן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: and our Tanna agrees with Rabbi Yehuda in one matter
and disagrees with him in one matter.
He agrees with Rabbi Yehuda in one matter:
about hot water and cooked food, and about taking off and putting back.
And he disagrees with him in one matter:
for our Tanna holds one may leave food

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ גָּרוּף וְקָטוּם,
phrases.english: even though the stove is not swept or covered,
while Rabbi Yehuda holds that for leaving too,

phrases.aramaic: גָּרוּף וְקָטוּם — אִין, אִי לָא — לָא.
phrases.english: if swept or covered, yes; if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by finding a תנא who fits the משנה read as being about returning. This defeats the proof for לשהות from steps 5-7, but it does not decide the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial-agreement answer: the תנא follows רבי יהודה in one matter and disagrees in another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the משנה is about returning, it contradicts both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, so no תנא fits it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה on hot water, cooked food, and taking off and returning. It disagrees only by allowing food to be left even on a stove that is not swept.

steps.title: May one lean a pot against an unswept stove?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: is it allowed to lean a pot against the side of a stove that is not swept or covered?
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars asked: what is the law about leaning a pot against the stove? Maybe only putting it inside or on top is forbidden, but leaning it against the side is fine. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks whether leaning a pot against the side of an unswept stove is treated like putting it on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that placing food inside or on top of an unswept stove is a problem. Leaning against the side is a weaker kind of contact with the heat. So maybe it is allowed. Or maybe the rabbis did not make any difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
To lean a pot against the side of the stove
Inside it and on top of it
It is fine, permitted
Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: They asked: what is the law about leaning against it?
Is only inside it and on top of it forbidden,
but leaning against it is fine,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about leaning a pot against the stove. The earlier debate (לשהות or להחזיר) ended with the 'returning' reading defended, not proven.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether leaning a pot against an unswept, uncovered stove is allowed, or whether it is forbidden just like putting it on top or inside.

steps.title: Proof from two stoves joined together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that leaning is allowed. A ברייתא permits leaving food on a swept stove even when it is joined to an unswept one that sends heat over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: with two stoves joined together, one swept or covered and one not, one may leave food on top of the swept one. This is true even though heat rises to it from the other stove.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא of the two joined stoves to answer the question. It argues that this shows getting heat from the side of an unswept stove is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pot on the swept stove still receives heat from the unswept stove next to it. That is like a pot leaning against an unswept stove. Since the ברייתא allows it, leaning should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a proof
Stoves that are joined together
Heat
From the other one

phrases.english: Come and hear: two stoves joined together,
one swept and covered
and one not swept and covered,
one may leave food on top of the swept and covered one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָא סָלֵיק לֵיהּ הַבְלָא מֵאִידָךְ!
phrases.english: Even though heat rises to it from the other one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That leaning against an unswept stove is allowed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of two joined stoves, which allows food on the swept one even though heat comes from the unswept one

steps.title: The joined stoves case is different because the pot is raised up
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. On top of the stove the pot is raised up, and air cools it. So it cannot be compared to a pot leaning right against the side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that case is different. Since the pot is raised up, the air reaches it and cools it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 10. It points out a real difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot on top of the swept stove gets only a little heat from its neighbor, because air around it cools it. A pot leaning right against an unswept stove gets much more heat. So permission in the first case says nothing about the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is different there
It is raised up
The air

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
since it is raised up, the air reaches it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question of leaning is answered later, in step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases are not alike. A raised pot is cooled by air, but a pot leaning against the stove is not.

steps.title: Proof from רב חייא's teaching about a stove that reignited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove that leaning needs a covered stove. רב חייא listed leaning as permitted only for a stove whose coals were covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב ספרא said in the name of רב חייא: if one covered the coals and they flared up again, one may lean a pot against it, leave food on it, take food off it, and put food back on it. Learn from this that leaning too is allowed only if one covered the coals, and not if one did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second attempt to answer the question. It infers from רב חייא's words that leaning is allowed only on a covered stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חייא lists leaning together with the other activities, all said about a stove that had been covered. This suggests that if the stove was not covered, leaning would be forbidden. That would mean leaning is treated like putting the pot on top.

keyTerms.meaning: He covered its coals with ashes
It flared up again
Leave food standing on it
Learn from this

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Safra said in the name of Rav Chiyya:
If one covered it and it flared up again,
one may lean a pot against it and leave food on it,
and take food off it and put food back on it.
Learn from this about leaning too:
if he covered it, yes; if he did not cover it, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב סָפְרָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a second proof for the question of step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That leaning against an uncovered stove is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חייא's teaching, which lists leaning among the activities allowed on a covered stove

steps.title: Leaning was listed only to go along with leaving
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Taking food off is allowed even from an uncovered stove, yet רב חייא listed it anyway. So the list does not prove that every item needs a covered stove. Some items are just paired with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your reasoning, does 'one may take food off it' also mean only if he covered it, and not if he did not?! Rather, he taught 'taking off' only because of 'putting back.' Here too, he taught 'leaning' only because of 'leaving.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 12. It shows that רב חייא's list includes an item that is allowed even on an uncovered stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that taking food off a stove is always allowed. It appears in the list only as a partner to 'putting back.' In the same way, 'leaning' may appear only as a partner to 'leaving,' so no rule about leaning can be learned. The next step challenges this comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turns the other side's logic against it
That he taught
He taught this item because of that item, as a paired partner

steps.whatToRemember: So far both proofs about leaning have been pushed off. The joined stoves are different because of the air, and רב חייא may have listed leaning only as a partner to leaving. The next step challenges this second push-off, and step 16 finally settles the question.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רב חייא's list as saying every item depends on covering the coals. 'Taking off' is in the list even though it is always allowed. Items can be listed just because they pair with another item.

phrases.english: And by your reasoning, what he taught, 'one may take off it':
if he covered it, yes; if he did not cover it, no?!
Rather, he taught 'taking off' because of 'putting back';

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא סוֹמְכִין מִשּׁוּם מְקַיְּימִין.
phrases.english: here too, he taught 'leaning' because of 'leaving.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רב חייא. It does not decide the law of leaning either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes every item in the list depends on covering the coals. 'Taking off' shows that some items are listed only to pair with another item.

steps.title: Why the comparison to taking food off does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the push-off from step 13. Taking off and putting back happen in the same place, so it makes sense to list them together. Leaning and leaving happen in different places, so pairing them must mean they share the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, taking off and putting back happen in one place, so the ברייתא mentioned taking off because of putting back. But here, leaning is in one place and leaving is in a different place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the push-off in step 13. It says the case of taking off food is not like the case of leaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot put a pot back before you take it off, and both happen on top of the same stove. So listing them together is natural, even if only one of them needs a covered stove. Leaning happens against the side and leaving happens on top, so there is no reason to list them together unless leaning also needs a covered stove. This brings back the proof from step 12, but it is only a strong hint, not a full proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?! (a cry of surprise that rejects a comparison)
we take off (a pot from the stove)
we put back (a pot onto the stove)
in one place

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'בחד מקום הוא' is said twice. The first time, about taking off and putting back, it means 'the same place.' The second time, about leaning and leaving, it means 'one place… and another place.' The words are the same, but the meaning is opposite.

phrases.english: Is that so?! (How can you compare?)
There, taking off and putting back
are in one and the same place,
so it taught taking off because of putting back.
But here —
leaning is in one place
phrases.notes: Against the side of the stove.

phrases.english: and leaving is in another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the push-off of step 13 and brings back the proof from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that leaning was just listed alongside leaving, the way taking off is listed alongside putting back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking off and putting back are linked because they happen in the same place. Leaning and leaving happen in different places, so the only reason to pair them is that they share the same rule.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The proofs and push-offs have not settled the question, so the גמרא asks for the final conclusion about leaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The back-and-forth has not settled the question, so the גמרא asks what the final ruling is. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 gave a strong hint, but not a full proof. So the question from step 9 is still open, and the גמרא now looks for a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: what
came out / is (the result)
about it (this question)

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 14 did not fully settle the question, the גמרא asks for the final answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it allowed to lean a pot against a stove that is not swept or covered?

steps.title: A ברייתא allows leaning against any stove
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that you may lean a pot against any stove. You may leave a pot on top only if the stove is swept or covered. Dimmed coals, or coals covered with thin flax waste, count as covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a stove that was lit with olive waste or with wood — we may lean a pot against it. But we may not leave a pot on it unless it is swept or covered with ashes. Coals that dimmed, or coals with a thin layer of flax waste placed on them, count as covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says clearly that leaning is allowed against any stove, and only leaving needs a swept or covered stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two separate rules: leaning is allowed with no condition, but leaving needs גרופה or קטומה. This settles the question from step 9: leaning is allowed even against an uncovered stove. The ברייתא also adds that dimmed coals, or coals under thin flax waste, already count as covered.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source is brought)
a stove (one with room for two pots)
olive waste left after pressing (makes a strong, hot fire)
dimmed, became faint
flax waste, the loose bits left from beating flax

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: you may lean a pot against any stove (סומכין). Leaving a pot on top (מקיימין) needs a stove that is גרופה or קטומה. Dimmed coals count as קטומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical answer about leaning a pot against a stove on שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A stove that was lit with olive waste or with wood
— we may lean a pot against it,
but we may not leave a pot on it unless
it is swept out or covered with ashes.
Coals that dimmed
or that someone placed on it
a thin layer of flax waste —
it is like a covered stove.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כִּירָה שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהָ בְּגֶפֶת וּבְעֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaning is allowed against any stove. Only leaving a pot on top needs a swept or covered stove.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא (תוספתא) about a stove lit with olive waste or wood

steps.title: A covered stove that flared up again
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני quotes רב אושעיא. If a stove was covered and then started burning again, you may still leave water or food on it, as long as it is already fully cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני said in the name of רב אושעיא: If someone covered the stove and it flared up again, we may leave on it hot water that is fully heated and food that is fully cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It deals with a stove that was covered with ashes but caught fire again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, leaving food on a burning stove is forbidden. The worry is that a person might stir the coals to cook the food more. Here the food is already fully cooked, so there is no reason to stir the coals, and leaving it is allowed even though the fire came back.

keyTerms.meaning: he covered it with ashes and it flared up again
we may leave (food on the stove)
hot water
fully, as much as it needs (fully cooked)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reason behind the whole rule: the worry is stirring the coals. When the food needs no more cooking, that worry goes away.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani said
that Rav Oshaya said:
If he covered it with ashes and it flared up again,
we may leave on it
hot water that was fully heated
and food that was fully cooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the leaning question is settled, a new teaching opens about a covered stove that flared up again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a covered stove flared up again, you may still leave hot water or food on it, as long as it is already fully cooked.
